meta.title: Northstar Attribution Comparison (TEST)
meta.subtitle: Historical, ex ante and simulated lanes ? governed server comparison

executive.bottom_line: Historical, ex ante, and simulated effects are compatible, and governed comparison metrics are available [S2][S3][S4][S5].

sections.title: Executive Comparison
sections.kicker: Two governed lanes are available without server comparison metrics

blocks.title: Key judgment — Historical
blocks.text: Observation: Historical effects are returned [S2]. Why it matters: Realized sources can be described. Uncertainty: One period may not persist. What would change the view: A later governed period.

blocks.title: Key judgment — Ex ante
blocks.text: Observation: Ex ante effects are returned [S3]. Why it matters: Expected sources can be described. Uncertainty: Inputs are assumptions. What would change the view: Refreshed governed inputs.

blocks.title: Key judgment — Comparison
blocks.text: Observation: Comparison capability is unavailable [S1]. Why it matters: Persistence cannot be assessed. Uncertainty: A future tool may return metrics. What would change the view: Published capability.

sections.title: Scope and Compatibility
sections.kicker: Portfolio, benchmark, cohort and currency identifiers match

sections.title: Historical Attribution
sections.kicker: Returned realized effects are shown without recalculation

blocks.title: Analysis — Selection leads detractors
blocks.text: Observation: Returned selection is negative [S2]. Why it matters: Selection leads realized detractors. Uncertainty: The evidence covers one linked period. What would change the view: A later historical result.

sections.title: Governed Ex Ante Attribution
sections.kicker: Returned expected effects are shown as assumptions

blocks.title: Analysis — Allocation leads expectations
blocks.text: Observation: Returned allocation is positive [S3]. Why it matters: Allocation leads expected effects. Uncertainty: Inputs are assumptions. What would change the view: A refreshed ex ante result.

items.name: Lane identity
items.note: Portfolio, cohort, currency and basis preserved [S4]

blocks.title: Analysis — Scenario effects returned
blocks.text: Observation: Simulated allocation is positive [S4]. Why it matters: Scenario attribution is available. Uncertainty: Results depend on governed scenario inputs. What would change the view: A revised simulation result.

sections.title: Cross-Lane Comparison
sections.kicker: Governed comparison returns compatible cross-lane metrics

blocks.title: Analysis — Lanes differ in sign
blocks.text: Observation: Returned lane signs differ [S5]. Why it matters: Realized and expected sources are not interchangeable. Uncertainty: Each lane uses a distinct governed basis. What would change the view: A refreshed comparison receipt.

sections.title: Coverage and Limitations
sections.kicker: Two live lanes and two capability gaps define coverage

blocks.title: Method boundary
blocks.text: Each lane remains on its returned method, period or horizon, benchmark role, parent cohort and calculation currency. Historical evidence is realized, ex ante evidence is expected, and simulated evidence is scenario-based. Values are displayed without local reconciliation, attribution arithmetic or substitutions [S1][S2][S3].

blocks.title: Comparison boundary
blocks.text: Cross-lane differences, concentration, overlap, reconciliation and persistence are reported only when the governed comparison capability returns them. Capability absence is an evidence limitation, not a zero value or a failed lane. Request IDs, diagnostics, residuals and coverage remain attached to their source payloads [S1].
